22. The Windrush scandal came to public attention in April 2018, but its fallout had been taking
place for many years before that, with a still unknown number of people affected. The
Windrush generation entered the UK from the Caribbean between 1948 and 1973; they had
the right of abode in the UK under the Immigration Act 1971, but they were not given any
confirmatory documents, and the Home Office did not keep accurate records.

23. After a tightening of immigration policy from 2012, members of the Windrush generation who
could not prove their legal status faced very significant detriment in relation to access to
housing, work and services (including NHS care), and in some cases even separation from
family, detention and removal from the UK. In March 2020, an independent review
